standards.name: Dublin Core Metadata Element Set, Version 1.1 (the fifteen-element Dublin Core)
standards.abstract: The Dublin Core describes metadata for generic resources (web pages, documents, images, datasets and other information objects) intended to support resource discovery across domains. Metadata values are typically expressed as textual properties (e.g. strings, keywords, identifiers) and used in Web and Linked Data contexts; Dublin Core is commonly embedded in records, HTML, XML or RDF descriptions. The specification presented here is the fifteen-element 'simple Dublin Core' reference (Version 1.1), maintained by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (DCMI) and endorsed in standards such as RFC 5013, ANSI/NISO Z39.85, and CEN CWA 13874. It addresses pragmatic interoperability by defining a stable set of fifteen element names, labels and natural-language definitions intended for broad, cross-disciplinary use and for combination in application profiles.

classification.rationale: The source material presents an explicit, named element set (15 named metadata elements) with per-element labels and formal definitions and (in the CWA) recorded datatype and other data-element attributes. This is a field-level metadata element set (a genuine table-like structure) rather than purely prose guidance or a procedural DAG.

standards.notes: CWA 13874 and RFC 5013 / RFC 2413 document the fifteen-element Dublin Core as Version 1.1. The CWA notes a common datatype attribute (Character String) and that each element is optional and repeatable; implementers often constrain usage in application profiles.

standards.name: DCMI Metadata Terms (Dublin Core)
standards.abstract: The standard covers metadata terms used to describe digital resources and other information objects, expressed primarily as RDF vocabularies for use in Linked Data but also applicable in XML/JSON/UML/relational encodings. It is an authoritative specification maintained by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative (DCMI) and curated by the DCMI Usage Board; it enumerates the fifteen core Dublin Core elements plus a larger set of properties, classes, syntax encoding schemes, and vocabulary encoding schemes, and explains namespace practice and usage guidance for application profiles and Linked Data publishing.

classification.rationale: The source is a prose specification and guidance document (an RDF vocabulary specification and usage guidance). Although it lists many named terms, the excerpted material presents them as a vocabulary and usage guidance rather than a concrete row/column metadata table with explicit per-field data types or a linear process (DAG). Therefore it fits the 'principle' category (prose guidance and specification) rather than 'table' or 'dag'.

principles.principle: This document is the authoritative, up-to-date specification of DCMI metadata terms, including properties, vocabulary encoding schemes, syntax encoding schemes, and classes.
principles.evidence: This document is an up-to-date specification of all metadata terms maintained by the Dublin Core Metadata Initiative, including properties, vocabulary encoding schemes, syntax encoding schemes, and classes.

principles.principle: DCMI metadata terms are expressed in RDF vocabularies for use in Linked Data, but may also be used in non-RDF encodings (XML, JSON, UML, relational databases) by disregarding RDF-specific formalities.
principles.evidence: DCMI metadata terms are expressed in RDF vocabularies for use in Linked Data. Creators of non-RDF metadata can use the terms in contexts such as XML, JSON, UML, or relational databases by disregarding both the global identifier and the formal implications of the RDF-specific aspects of term definitions.

principles.principle: Each term is identified with a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), i.e., a global identifier intended for Linked Data use.
principles.evidence: Each term is identified with a Uniform Resource Identifier (URI), a global identifier usable in Linked Data.

principles.principle: DCMI uses a small set of namespaces (including /elements/1.1/ and /terms/) and documents the distinction and usage guidance for them (including the presence of parallel properties and formal ranges).
principles.evidence:
The four DCMI namespaces are:
http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/
The /elements/1.1/ namespace was created in 2000 for the RDF representation of the fifteen-element Dublin Core and has been widely used in data for more than twenty years. This namespace corresponds to the original scope of ISO 15836, which was published first in 2003 and last revised in 2017 as ISO 15836-1:2017 [
ISO 15836-1:2017
.
http://purl.org/dc/terms/
The /terms/ namespace was originally created in 2001 for identifying new terms coined outside of the original fifteen-element Dublin Core. In 2008, in the context of defining formal semantic constraints for DCMI metadata terms in support of RDF applications, the original fifteen elements themselves were mirrored in the /terms/ namespace.  As a result, there exists both a dc:date (http://purl.org/dc/elements/1.1/date) with no formal range and a corresponding dcterms:date (http://purl.org/dc/terms/date) with a formal range of "literal".

principles.principle: The specification includes the fifteen-element Dublin Core (the core elements) as part of the terms, and lists them explicitly in the /elements/1.1/ namespace.

standards.notes: The source material is a vocabulary specification and usage guidance; full per-term machine-readable datatypes and formal domain/range information are provided in the authoritative RDF schemas linked from the specification. This extraction captures the specification's main guidance/principles and the explicit listing of the fifteen core elements present in the supplied excerpts.
